data.narrative:
Quaise Energy, founded by Carlos Araque and Matthew Houde, is a Series A–stage climate and energy company that has raised $134M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector comprises 8 private peers and 1 public comparable (Lenza, ticker LNZA), though no private peers share identical stage and valuation positioning.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable approach. Using total capital raised ($134M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $268M. Peer-median triangulation was not viable; while 8 same-sector peers exist (including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix), none satisfied minimum thresholds for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier clustering. A single-method analysis carries execution risk.

The available data supports a valuation range of $228M to $308M, centered on a $268M median. This reflects conservative bounds around the stage-progression result, with the low and high figures representing ±15% variance. Key uncertainties include the absence of a robust narrow-peer set for cross-validation and reliance on raised capital as a valuation proxy, which may not reflect technology maturity, path to commercialization, or sector-specific capital intensity. Additional due diligence on comparable exits and revenue multiples within the energy transition space would strengthen conviction.
